extracted.intended_audience: Congressional Appropriations Committees; HHS/NIH officials; ARPA-H leadership, program managers, and stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Official FY2024 Congressional Justification for the Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health describing mission, budget request, program design principles, staffing, performance management, and funding authorities. Provides criteria and guidance for program selection, management, transition, and agency operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with ARPA-H mission
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects and programs must accelerate better health outcomes for everyone and advance high-potential, high-impact biomedical and health research that cannot be readily accomplished through traditional research or commercial activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs should be disease-agnostic when appropriate and aim to produce transformative solutions that benefit the American people; preference for efforts that remove limitations that stymie progress toward broadly applicable solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: ARPA-H-hard problem design (Heilmeier 2 / ARPA-H-hard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Design programs that are 'ARPA-Hard' and well-defined problems in health using the Heilmeier 2 framework to outline high risk/high consequences and identify those appropriately 'ARPA-hard' with potential for high impact aligned with the agency mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Heilmeier-derived questions should be used to define problems, show why they cannot be readily addressed through traditional research or commercial activities, and articulate the high-risk/high-reward rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of adapted Heilmeier questions
rubrics_metrics.description: ARPA-H has adopted and enhanced the Heilmeier questions to guide PMs, incorporating tenets of broad population relevance, equity, and real-world applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Heilmeier responses are requested during hiring and program formulation to ensure PMs and programs begin with directional focus increasing likelihood of success; the adapted questions are central to both hiring and program planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Manager (PM) selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Recruit PMs who 'have a track record for being action and application oriented in their field', with demonstrated expertise (or boldness to take on a new field) and a passion for solving big problems in health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Heilmeier answers are used in hiring; PMs should bring unique vision, be capable of building multidisciplinary teams, and be committed to time-bound, milestone-driven execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitive selection of performers/teams
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a competitive process to identify optimal industry and academic partners to help solve the greatest challenges to the health ecosystem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage federal expertise for input, amplify opportunities through networks, minimize duplication, and assemble the most compelling performer teams to deliver solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metrics-driven program execution
rubrics_metrics.description: Execute and measure programs with active program management against metrics; PMs will monitor progress against metrics, budget performance, and pivot resources as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs are expected to have technical milestones aligned to program and budget checkpoints; monthly, quarterly, and annual reviews will examine progress and budget execution; metrics should support evidence-based decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-bound and milestone-driven programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Mission activities and programs will be time-bound and milestone-driven, with clear 'mid-term' and 'final' exams to evaluate progress and success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most programs proceed in phases. PMs work with leadership to develop plans with technical milestones; high-touch oversight facilitates early identification of failures and redirection of resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition and commercialization as success criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Success includes transition of programs and capabilities out of the agency once the intended capability is demonstrated and the investment is de-risked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transition pathways may include securing downstream public/private funding, company formation, licensing, or engagement with customers and investors; ARPA-H will mentor PMs and make connections to support downstream adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real-world impact / 'survive in the wild'
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs should lead to measurably improved health outcomes in the real world through tools, technologies, and therapeutics that reach customers — the American people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ARPA-H values solutions that are adopted by end-users and continue beyond ARPA-H funding; program evaluation emphasizes real-world adoption and measurable outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equity and broad population relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Program design and selection must incorporate equity and broad population relevance ensuring solutions are accessible and equitable for all people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ARPA-H adapted evaluation tenets to include equity and encourages stakeholder engagement (patients, caregivers, communities) to understand practical considerations across groups and populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-redundancy and coordination with federal partners
rubrics_metrics.description: ARPA-H will seek stakeholder insights and partner with federal and community networks to validate that efforts are not redundant and significantly advance the state of the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs should be coordinated to minimize duplication across government, leverage existing infrastructure, and complement other agencies' work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for platform/capability investments with wide applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Make big bets to build high-payoff capabilities or platforms to drive biomedical breakthroughs that provide transformative solutions across a broad range of diseases and scales.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work may range from molecular to societal scales; emphasis on technologies or platforms that enable many downstream applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active stakeholder engagement throughout lifecycle
rubrics_metrics.description: PMs will foster stakeholder engagement throughout program life cycle to ensure programs can transition out of the agency and be sustained by other funders or the commercial marketplace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage patients, providers, advocacy groups, industry, academia, and federal agencies; ARPA-H expects PMs to involve stakeholders early and often.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-touch program oversight and review cadence
rubrics_metrics.description: PMs and agency leadership will conduct monthly, quarterly, and annual reviews; employ mid-term and final exams; and track budget execution to rapidly identify and address failures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frequent communication with performers and active management enable pivots and resource redirection to maximize promising efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term limits for PMs to create urgency and discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: ARPA-H defines term limits for PMs to create urgency and discipline needed to drive development and implementation of health solutions at the 'speed of relevancy.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fixed-term PM appointments are an organizational parameter to infuse fresh perspective and focus on deliverables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staffing and workforce model constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: ARPA-H will employ a limited number of full-time federal workforce members (maximum 210 per Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023), with nearly half as PMs, augmented by a supporting contractor team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency must recruit within FTE caps, leverage contractors for nimbleness, and pursue solicitation to build contractor workforce for mission-critical activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexible funding and award authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: ARPA-H has authority to make awards in the form of grants, contracts, cooperative agreements, cash prizes, and enter into other transactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the appropriate instrument to accelerate results; appropriation language and allocation methods permit varied award types to suit program needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance metrics and KPIs for organizational and program decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop metrics-driven systems, key performance indicators, evidence-based tracking, and transparent reporting structures to evaluate projects and activities and inform organizational decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ARPA-H is developing its strategic plan and expects to determine performance metrics (outputs and outcomes table) after establishing initial programs; dashboards, integrated data management, and governance are anticipated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiscal stewardship and risk management
rubrics_metrics.description: Build effective financial stewardship and risk management functions that foster prudent use of resources and maintain public trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stand up operations to deliver accurate, transparent, and on-time financial reports and justifications, document standard business processes, and implement integrated data solutions for end-to-end program tracking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of horizon scans and public-private partnerships to identify opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify emergent opportunities through advanced systematic horizon scans of academic and industry efforts and leverage novel public-private partnerships for rapid progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine directive approaches for quick funding decisions with horizon scanning to surface high-impact ideas and seize emergent opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program planning with technical milestones aligned to budget checkpoints
rubrics_metrics.description: PMs will develop specific plans with technical milestones that align to program and budget checkpoints to facilitate phase progression and evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plans should define phases, mid-term/final assessments, resources required, and criteria for pivot/termination decisions tied to budget execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition network and partnership intermediaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish transition teams and partnership intermediary agreements (PIA) to identify transition partners and promote awareness of ARPA-H for downstream adoption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PIAs and outreach to patient and advocacy groups and formal contracts with intermediaries to support commercialization, transition planning, and early engagement for sustainability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection validation against redundancy and state-of-the-art advancement
rubrics_metrics.description: Validate proposed efforts with stakeholders to ensure they are not redundant and that they significantly advance the state of the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection processes should include external input and mapping to existing efforts to justify ARPA-H investment on grounds of uniqueness and potential impact.
